questions.q: What is TOGAF, and who maintains it?
options: A certification exam for security architects, maintained by ISACA
A European data protection regulation, maintained by the EU
The Open Group Architecture Framework, maintained by The Open Group, an industry consortium
A vendor-specific architecture tool sold by a single software company
questions.explain: TOGAF stands for The Open Group Architecture Framework and is maintained by The Open Group, a vendor-neutral industry consortium — it's the most widely adopted enterprise architecture framework in use.

questions.q: What are TOGAF's four architecture domains, commonly abbreviated BDAT?
options: Business, Data, Application, Technology
Backup, Development, Audit, Testing
Budget, Design, Approval, Training
Baseline, Diagram, Artifact, Template
questions.explain: BDAT stands for Business, Data, Application, and Technology architecture — the four domains TOGAF organizes enterprise architecture work around.

options: Application Deployment Model — a tool for deploying software to production
Annual Development Metrics — a yearly scorecard for IT project performance
Access Decision Matrix — a table defining who can approve architecture changes
Architecture Development Method — a cyclical, lettered process (Phases A through H) for developing and governing architecture
questions.explain: The ADM, or Architecture Development Method, is TOGAF's engine: a cyclical, iterative method with phases A through H wrapped around central Requirements Management.

questions.q: Why isn't security one of TOGAF's four BDAT domains?
options: Because TOGAF considers security to be entirely out of scope for enterprise architecture
Because security was deliberately replaced by compliance as the fifth domain in a later TOGAF version
Because The Open Group treats security, along with risk, as a cross-cutting concern addressed inside every ADM phase rather than confined to one domain
Because TOGAF assumes every organization already has a separate security framework and doesn't need its own guidance
questions.explain: The Open Group's TOGAF Series Guide: Integrating Risk and Security treats security as a cross-cutting concern that must be addressed within every ADM phase, not as a dedicated fifth domain.

questions.q: How are SABSA and TOGAF typically described when used together?
options: As competing frameworks that an organization must choose between and never combine
As TOGAF supplying the overall process and governance cadence, while SABSA supplies the business-traceable security content that fills it in
As identical frameworks published under two different names by the same organization
As SABSA replacing TOGAF entirely once security maturity reaches a certain level
questions.explain: SABSA is a content framework (what security architecture should contain) and TOGAF is a process framework (how the architecture practice runs); joint guidance shows SABSA's layers populating the security content inside TOGAF's ADM phases.
